cycles.title: Cycle Views
cycles.description: Audience-specific views over the APIOps Cycles method graph.
cycle.capability-productization-cycle.de: A cycle for turning business capabilities into reusable digital capabilities before selecting the implementation style.
cycle.capability-productization-cycle.pu: Identify and productize reusable digital capabilities before deciding whether the delivery style should be APIs, events, files, streams, data products, AI-enabled services, direct integration, or a hybrid pattern.
cycle.api-productization-cycle.title: API Productization Cycle
cycle.api-productization-cycle.descripti: The API-focused APIOps Cycles journey for productizing, designing, delivering, publishing, and improving APIs.
cycle.api-productization-cycle.purpose: API-focused method journey for teams that already know the intended delivery style is an API product.
cycle.integration-productization-cycle.d: A cycle for productizing reusable integration capabilities before selecting a concrete integration pattern.
cycle.integration-productization-cycle.p: Guide reusable integration capability design before choosing APIs, events, files, streams, data products, direct integration, or hybrid patterns.
cycle.capability-productization-cycle.st: Before building anything, define your API’s value, users, and business goals from day one.
Capture consumer requirements, onboarding needs, constraints, service expectations, and producer responsibilities.
Use requirements and constraints to choose architecture and platform capabilities.
Design the selected solution mechanism and interface contract.
Deliver and operate the selected solution mechanism.
Assure quality, governance, and readiness before release.
Publish capability information so consumers can discover, request, onboard, and get support.
Monitor capability health, consumer outcomes, reliability, reuse, and improvement opportunities.
cycle.api-productization-cycle.station.a: Frame the API as a product with clear value proposition, consumers, business model, ownership, and lifecycle intent.
Define API consumer segments, onboarding paths, expectations, and experience requirements before design decisions are locked.
Choose and validate the API platform, architecture, governance, and operational constraints needed for the product.
Design the API contract, interaction model, schemas, policies, and usability details before implementation.
Implement, test, secure, automate, and operate the API product through the delivery pipeline.
Validate API quality, compliance, readiness, evidence, and release criteria before publication.
Publish the API product so consumers can discover, evaluate, request access, onboard, and get support.
cycle.api-productization-cycle.station.m: Monitor API health, adoption, consumer outcomes, reliability, and improvement opportunities after release.
cycle.integration-productization-cycle.s: Frame the reusable integration capability, business need, ownership, and expected reuse before selecting a pattern.
Capture integration consumers, provider responsibilities, onboarding needs, service expectations, and operational constraints.
Decide the integration architecture, platform capabilities, constraints, and governance model for the capability.
Design the integration solution, contracts, payloads, events, APIs, files, or interaction patterns selected for the capability.
Build, test, automate, deploy, and operate the integration capability across its selected delivery pattern.
Assure integration readiness, governance, quality, security, compliance, and operational evidence before release.
Publish the integration capability so teams can discover, request, reuse, onboard, and get support.
Monitor integration reliability, reuse, incidents, performance, consumer outcomes, and improvement needs.
cycle.automation-cycle.title: Automation Cycle
cycle.automation-cycle.description: A cycle for identifying, designing, delivering, enabling, and improving automation opportunities.
cycle.automation-cycle.purpose: Productize automation opportunities into governed workflows with clear users, platforms, controls, delivery paths, enablement, and monitoring.
cycle.automation-cycle.station.api-produ: Identify and prioritize automation opportunities by value, feasibility, risk, ownership, and expected process impact.
cycle.automation-cycle.station.api-consu: Capture process users, roles, handoffs, exceptions, constraints, and service expectations before designing the automation.
cycle.automation-cycle.station.api-platf: Choose the automation platform, runtime, integration model, governance controls, and operational constraints.
cycle.automation-cycle.station.api-desig: Design the automation workflow, triggers, decision points, integrations, data handling, and exception paths.
cycle.automation-cycle.station.api-deliv: Build, test, deploy, document, and operate the automation with clear ownership and rollback paths.
cycle.automation-cycle.station.api-audit: Review automation readiness, quality, risk, compliance, human oversight, evidence, and release criteria.
cycle.automation-cycle.station.api-publi: Enable users and operators with discovery, onboarding, operating instructions, support paths, and change communication.
cycle.automation-cycle.station.monitorin: Monitor automation performance, exceptions, reliability, user outcomes, operational impact, and improvement opportunities.
